excerpts.text: The [Nobel Prize in Chemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Chemistry "Nobel Prize in Chemistry") ([Swedish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swedish_language "Swedish language"): *Nobelpriset i kemi*) is awarded annually by the [Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Swedish_Academy_of_Sciences "Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences") to scientists in the various fields of [chemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemistry "Chemistry").

Two others have won Nobel Prizes twice, one in chemistry and one in another subject: [Maria Skłodowska-Curie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marie_Curie "Marie Curie") (physics in 1903, chemistry in 1911) and [Linus Pauling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linus_Pauling "Linus Pauling") (chemistry in 1954, peace in 1962).[[6]](#cite_note-6) As of 2025, the prize has been awarded to 200 individuals, including eight women (Maria Skłodowska-Curie being the first to be awarded in 1911).[[7]](#cite_note-nobelprize.org-7)
